The commit message says new login sessions lose the retained name because "store is cleared on logout", but logout does not clear the virtual media store in Authentication.js

Fixed. Added a `clearDevices` mutation to VirtualMediaStore that resets
proxyDevices and legacyDevices to empty arrays. This mutation is now called
from the logout action in AuthenticanStore immediately after the auth state
is cleared, so the commit message claim is accurate.
This looking good, I noticed the Stop button issue when testing.

Done

This is pragmatic, and ok for now (and was my suggestion..).
Please put a note here: "FIXME: Vuex state is now explicitly carrying non-serializable browser objects, better done in a composable"
The store builds proxy devices from the Redfish `Inserted` state, but those devices have `file: null` and `no nbd` object.

Fixed. nbd: null is now included in all three proxy device construction paths:
- The fallback return in setProxyDevicesData (when device is not active)
- The default single-device path in getData (VITE_VIRTUAL_MEDIA_LIST_ENABLED=false)
- The .map() for the list-enabled Redfish path in getData

All proxy devices now have a consistent shape regardless of how they are built.

this skips `getData` whenever existing store state is present.
Ensure this store info is deleted on logout/loss of session.

Fixed in two parts:
1. Removed the early-return guard from created() — getData always fetches
   fresh Redfish state on every page entry.
2. The new clearDevices mutation is called on logout, so stale device state
   is never carried into a new login session.

stopVM still assumes a browser-created NbdServer exists.

If the BMC reports a proxy device as inserted after a refresh, reconnect, or another UI session, the Stop button is enabled and clicking it throws Cannot read properties of undefined/null (reading 'stop').

Recommendation: only enable browser-proxy Stop when dev.nbd exists, or make stopVM defensive and present an explanatory state for active media that cannot be stopped by the current browser session. If there is a Redfish eject path for this state, use that instead.

Fixed. Both parts of the recommendation are addressed:

1. The browser-proxy Stop button now uses v-if="dev.isActive && dev.nbd" —
   it is only rendered when the current browser session owns the NBD
   connection, preventing the crash entirely.

2. When isActive=true and nbd=null (device reported as Inserted by the BMC
   but no browser-owned connection exists — e.g. another UI session or a
   BMC that retains Inserted state), the card now shows an informational
   label "Active in another session" and a separate Stop button that calls
   the Redfish EjectMedia action (unmountImage) to eject the media cleanly.
   stopVM() also has a defensive early-return guard as a belt-and-suspenders
   measure.

Note: the specific BMC used for testing returns Inserted: false while a
WebSocket session is active, so the isActive && !nbd path is not triggered
in that environment. However the fix is correct and necessary for BMC
implementations that do return Inserted: true, which is the case the
reviewer encountered during testing.
